item.title: Federal judge considers whether to extend ban against U.S. Postal Service mail voting changes
item.description:
An election worker processes mail-in ballots at the Los Angeles County Ballot Processing Center during California’s state primary election in June. Patrick T. item.title: Spain’s PM says no evidence Morocco planned Ceuta border rush
item.description:
The government’s sluggish response has been disastrous for everyone involved – and for Sánchez’s message on immigration More than a month after an estimated 72,000 people suddenly crossed from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta, the city remains in chaos and the damage inflicted on the Spanish government is becoming clearer. Most of those who made the crossing have returned to Morocco. The scale of the incident was nevertheless extraordinary, and about 140 people are thought to have died . Also extraordinary was the response of the 22 EU governments that rounded on the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, rather than demonstrate the solidarity one might expect from allies. Perhaps less surprising was the exploitation of the crisis by rightwing and far-right parties in Spain and beyond, Donald Trump’s attacks and the interventions of Russian state-linked actors and Israeli…

item.title: Trump Is Back To Seeking Regime Change in Iran
item.description:
President Donald Trump's attack on Iran was clearly designed as a regime-change war. In his opening speech of the war, on February 28, he told "the great proud people of Iran" that "the hour of your freedom is at hand" and that everyone associated with the Iranian government was marked for "certain death," from generals to traffic cops. Trump told other leaders (and later admitted publicly ) that he expected the Islamic Republic to collapse in a few days. A little over a month into the war, with no signs of Iranian collapse, Trump changed his goals to securing a favorable deal with Iran, and eventually signed a U.S.-Iranian peace memorandum in June 2026. item.title: Stranded survivors in Nepal cross raging Trishuli River using zip line
item.description:
Nepali authorities have erected a makeshift zip line to help stranded residents travel across the swollen waters of the Trishuli river after last week’s deadly flash floods swept away bridges, leaving them cut off from the outside world. Some were in need of urgent treatment, medicines, food and other essentials.

Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24

item.title: Indonesia: Thousands fall sick from free school meals
item.description:
Hundreds of new food poisoning cases have been reported this week linked to President Prabowo Subianto's free school lunch program. The costly scheme has been dogged by health concerns and allegations of corruption.
